_comment: Run template for nist-heatpump-fdd: residential split heat pumps in a laboratory, one row per steady-state test point on a synthetic clock, so only a rule that reads the level of a steady point fits. It runs dx_refrigerant_charge (0.93) in target mode: each unit's cooling-mode median liquid subcooling against a target subcooling with the usual +/-3 F charging tolerance. The targets stand in for the nameplate charging targets, which the data do not publish: they are the fault-free runs' median subcooling per unit (8.6 F on the 14 SEER unit, 9.7 F on the 16 SEER unit), so the four fault-free runs are scored in-sample. min_samples is 1 because each row is already an averaged test point. `camber datasets score nist-heatpump-fdd` scores the charge detector against the charge-fault runs; the indoor-airflow detector compares a unit with its own fault-free period (the dx drift family) and cannot run across separate test runs from a config -- see docs/FDD-DX.md for its leave-one-file-out score. Every time-based rule would read the synthetic clock as time, so none is run.
